precepts.text: The Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue. They were kicking people out left and right.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.
precepts.why:
The temple kept money “laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children”, yet in Acts 6 the widows of the disciples were neglected in the daily ministration. Why couldn’t they get it from the temple? John shows what the priesthood had already decided.

The man born blind was healed, and his parents would not answer plainly: “These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.”

They were kicking people out left and right. So Peter and them saw that the widows were not getting anything from the temple, because they believed in Christ. Put out of the synagogue, they were cut off from the relief the temple held for widows and the fatherless.

That is why the apostles had to look out seven men of honest report to serve tables and take care of the widows themselves. And that is how the deacons came to be chosen.

precepts.text: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
precepts.point: The man born blind was not paying for his own sin; God used him to show his power. Do not presume on God's mercy and play with his judgment.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The disciples asked, “Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?” They were asking about something Christ had taught them, the regeneration. How could the man have sinned to be paying for it with blindness from birth, unless he was here before? Christ did not say, what are you talking about. He answered that in this case it was neither, “but that the works of God should be made manifest in him”.

But paying for the sins of the fathers is real, and Matthew 23 shows how it works. Christ tells the scribes and Pharisees, “ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity”. They “build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets”. They were saying, that wasn't us.

Christ answers: “Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”. They came back generations later proclaiming to be righteous, but they were the ones doing the killing back then. Fill ye up means reap what you sow: it's time to pay for what you did.

It works the same way for the nations and for us. Those who led us into captivity on the slave ships have not yet gone into captivity, but they are going, because they have to fill up the measure of their fathers. And we had to fill up the measure of ours: the same spirits Moses stood in front of at Sinai and told they would go back to Egypt in ships came back generations later and went on those ships.

precepts.text: Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and to the fourth generation.
precepts.point: The man born blind was not paying for his own sin; God used him to show his power. Do not presume on God's mercy and play with his judgment.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 makes it super clear. The Lord is “Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty”. The guilty were those that killed the prophets. He is “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation”.

The iniquity of the fathers was the murder of the prophets, and it was visited upon the children, the Pharisees of Christ's day. That is what Christ meant by “Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”: you were your fathers, doing the killing back then. Those born in the third and fourth generation pay for the sins committed three or four generations ago.

So the man born blind in John 9 was not paying for his own sin. The Most High caused him to be born blind so that he could be healed later, and the Lord may allow a situation anywhere so he can exercise his mercy and his power on it as an example to the rest of us. People needed to see that Christ could heal. The Lord has people's lives plotted out for what he needs them to be.

But that is not an excuse to do evil. Don't be so confident in his mercy that you go out and play with the Most High's judgment, because he will by no means clear the guilty, and you might not even make it in here.

precepts.text: Now we know that God heareth not sinners. Now, this is clear and plain. Now we know, everybody knows, that God heareth not sinners. So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers.
precepts.point: So when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard. So why does it say that? It means when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard. Showing that it is a commandment to honour your parents. Why is that? Why will your prayers not be heard?
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.” Why does it say that? It means that when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard, which shows that honouring your parents is a commandment.

John makes it clear and plain: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners”. Everybody knows it. Dishonouring your parents is breaking a commandment, and a sinner is not heard.

So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers. The one who honours his father is keeping the commandment, and that is why, when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.

precepts.text: God hears not sinners, but if any man be a worshiper of God and does His will, him He hears.
precepts.point: The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that He will not hear.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.” Why would the Most High seem asleep to our cry? “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.”

God hears not sinners. Our iniquities hid his face so that he will not hear; but if any man be a worshipper of God and does his will, him he hears. So the plea for him to arise for our help and redeem us is answered by doing his will, so that we are the ones he hears.

precepts.text: God heareth not sinners; a man after the Lord's own heart is a man that keeps the commandments, and the Lord deals with those that are Israel and keep His commandments.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.” David could say “Attend unto my cry” because a man after the Lord’s own heart is a man that keeps the commandments. The Lord deals with those that are Israel and keep his commandments, and to them he deals bountifully, and the righteous compass them about.

precepts.text: The Most High hears not sinners, but the worshipper that does his will.
precepts.point: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be an abomination, as John 9 says the Most High does not hear sinners.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.” Turn your ear from the law and even your prayer is an abomination.

John 9 says the same: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.” The Most High does not hear sinners; he hears the worshipper that does his will. The man who will not hear the law is the sinner whose prayer goes unheard.

So keeping the law is not separate from prayer. The wise son who keeps the law is the one whose prayer is heard.

precepts.text: The Most High does not hear sinners; He told Jeremiah not to pray for them because their sins were, and are, so many, which is why it behooves all of us to repent.
precepts.point: He tells Jeremiah not to pray for this people; even when they fast He will not hear their cry, and their offerings He will not accept, but will consume them by sword, famine and pestilence.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Jeremiah, “Pray not for this people for their good”, and says that when they fast he will not hear their cry. John gives the rule behind it: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.”

The people loved to wander and did not refrain their feet; their sins were so many that he would remember their iniquity and visit their sins. He told Jeremiah not to pray for them because their sins were, and are, so many. God does not hear sinners; he hears the man that worships him and does his will.

That is why it behooves all of us to repent. Fasting and offerings will not be heard from a people that keep wandering; he hears those that do his will.

precepts.text: After Christ healed on the sabbath day there was a division, some saying this man is not of God, and others saying how can a man that is a sinner do such miracles.
precepts.point: The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.” The Pharisees were divided over it: “Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them.”

Some could not get past the Sabbath; others could not get past the miracle. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works, the way the works of the apostles could not be denied by the whole council.
